new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Rensch (family-level, Land Dayak incl. the Southern Land Dayak varieties Kembayan, Ribun, Semandang): accent falls on the final syllable of the stem, most clearly in utterance-final position; no contrastive accent. Per the only Ribun-specific phonology (Simanjuntak & Bunau 2023): stress is not phonemic in Ribun; position not stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Rensch p.~4408 (Part I, Sarawak Bidayuh) notes that clitics take the word-final stress of their host in citation forms; not stated for Ribun.
new_statements.domain_note: Rensch: stem-final syllable, 'especially evident in utterance-final position' -- a generalization over 'the contemporary Land Dayak languages'; the authors' Ribun material is wordlists (Hudson 1970; Adelaar unpublished), so the claim is not independently verified for Ribun. Simanjuntak & Bunau: isolated citation forms (Swadesh-based 1100-item list) from Pusat Damai, Parindu.
new_statements.identity_note: Simanjuntak & Bunau 2023 describe Ribun of Pusat Damai (Parindu sub-district); Asfar 2017 Ribun/Hibun of the Tayan Hulu basin (local sub-labels Hibun Sobo', Hibun Dohit, Hibun Tudo); Sommerlot 2020 Ribun of Pandung (north bank of the Kapuas, Sanggau). All are ribu1241 (ISO rir; alternate name Hibun, from r > h). The positional (final-syllable) statement in Rensch et al. 2012 is a generalization over 'Land Dayak' (Bidayuh + Bakati' + Southern Land Dayak = Kembayan, Ribun, Semandang), held under the Biatah folder biat1246; it is first-hand prose but its Ribun basis is wordlist data only.

sources.note: Part III (C. Rensch, Proto Land Dayak) sec. 6.2.4, printed p.293: 'an accentual difference is not evident in the contemporary Land Dayak languages. They consistently accent the final syllable of the stem; this is especially evident in utterance-final position.' Ribun is one of the three Southern Land Dayak varieties in scope, but its Ribun data are Hudson 1970 plus Adelaar's unpublished wordlists (Sources of Data), so for Ribun this is a family-level generalization, not an observed fact. Part I p.64 (PDF) states ultima stress for Sarawak Bidayuh specifically.

sources.note: Ribun-specific phonemic description (fieldwork Pusat Damai, Parindu, 2022; 1100 lexemes). No statement of stress position; p.205: 'the phonemic of the RDL is segmental, not suprasegmental' and (Conclusions) 'There is no evidence that the phonemes are prosodic, involving rhythm, stress, and intonation' -- i.e. stress is not contrastive. Uses 'stressed/unstressed syllable' only in an allophone rule for /i/ copied from an Indonesian template.
